Three money questions most people get wrong. Can you answer them? You get three seconds each, and number three hurts the most.
Question one. Your money grows at eight percent a year. How many years until it doubles? Three. Two. One.
About nine years. Just divide seventy two by the rate. Seventy two divided by eight is nine. That's the rule of seventy two.
Got it? Now it gets harder. Prices rise six percent every year. After twelve years, what does a hundred rupees buy? Three. Two. One.
Only about fifty rupees worth. Seventy two divided by six is twelve. The same rule, now working against you. Your money halved, and you never spent it.
Final question, and this one hurts. Your investment falls fifty percent. How much must it rise to get back to where it started? Three. Two. One.
Most people say fifty. Here's a real clue. The Nifty is about fourteen percent below its January high. To get back there, it needs about sixteen percent, not fourteen.
So the answer is one hundred percent. One lakh falls to fifty thousand, and fifty thousand must double to become one lakh again. Big losses need even bigger gains.
